subject: chemistry
title: Fuel cells
key_idea: A hydrogen fuel cell is supplied with hydrogen and oxygen from outside. Hydrogen is oxidised to produce water and a potential difference. Water is the only product, and fuel cells can be compared with rechargeable cells and batteries.

sections.heading: How a hydrogen fuel cell works

blocks.text: (Separate science) This section covers what goes into a fuel cell and what comes out.

items.meaning: A cell supplied with a fuel, such as hydrogen, and oxygen or air from an external source, which reacts to produce a potential difference.
Reacted with oxygen, or losing electrons.

items: Hydrogen is the fuel. Oxygen comes from the air.
The fuel is **oxidised** electrochemically in the cell to produce a potential difference.
The overall reaction is the oxidation of hydrogen to produce water.

blocks.label: Overall reaction in a hydrogen fuel cell
where: H₂O is water, the only product

blocks.text: (Higher tier) At each electrode a half equation shows what happens. These are for an acidic electrolyte.

blocks.label: Positive electrode
where: oxygen reacts with hydrogen ions and electrons to form water

items: (Higher tier) For an alkaline electrolyte the half equations are H₂ + 2OH⁻ → 2H₂O + 2e⁻ and O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e⁻ → 4OH⁻.
Doubling the first half equation and adding the second gives the overall reaction.
A fuel cell is supplied with hydrogen and oxygen, and hydrogen is oxidised to water.
Overall: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, with water the only product.

sections.heading: Fuel cells compared with rechargeable cells

blocks.text: (Separate science) Hydrogen fuel cells offer a possible alternative to rechargeable cells and batteries, for example to power cars.

rows: Hydrogen and oxygen supplied from outside
Chemicals sealed in the cell; recharged by an external current
Voltage falls as the cell runs down
No toxic chemicals to dispose of
May release toxic chemicals on disposal

diagram.alt: Sort statements into advantages and disadvantages of a hydrogen fuel cell compared with a rechargeable cell.
diagram.prompt: Sort each statement into an advantage or a disadvantage of a hydrogen fuel cell.

items.text: It is faster to refuel than to recharge
It can travel further before refuelling
There are no toxic chemicals to dispose of at the end of its life
Hydrogen is made from fossil fuels, which are not renewable
Hydrogen is flammable and can be explosive
There are not many hydrogen filling stations

items: Hydrogen can be renewable if it is made by electrolysis using renewable energy.
A fuel cell keeps working as long as hydrogen and oxygen are supplied. A non-rechargeable cell stops when a reactant is used up.
When data is given, compare the values. Do not only restate them.
Finish an evaluation with a judgement and a reason.
Advantages: faster refuelling, longer range, only water produced, no toxic disposal.
Disadvantages: hydrogen is flammable, hard to store, often made from fossil fuels and few filling stations exist.

checks.q: (Separate science) Write the overall equation for the reaction in a hydrogen fuel cell.
(Separate science) Describe how a hydrogen fuel cell produces a potential difference.
checks.a: Hydrogen is oxidised (electrochemically) to produce water.

checks.q: (Separate science) Give one advantage and one disadvantage of a hydrogen fuel cell compared with a rechargeable cell.
checks.a: Advantage: faster to refuel, or travels further, or the only product is water. Disadvantage: hydrogen is made from fossil fuels, or is difficult to store, or is flammable.

exam_phrases: no toxic chemicals to dispose of at the end of the cell's life
hydrogen is made from fossil fuels / non-renewable resources
hydrogen is difficult to store; hydrogen is flammable / explosive; not many hydrogen filling stations

mistakes.right: No emissions and an unqualified expensive are ignored. Say the only product is water, and that it costs more to refuel or to manufacture.

mistakes.wrong: A fuel cell produces a potential difference because of its electrodes.
mistakes.right: References to electrodes are ignored. Say hydrogen is oxidised (it loses electrons) to produce water.

worked_example.question:
Hydrogen fuel cells or rechargeable cells can be used to power electric vehicles.

Suggest one advantage and one disadvantage of using a hydrogen fuel cell compared with a rechargeable cell.
answer_points: Advantage, any one from: faster to refuel (than recharging); can travel further (before refuelling); hydrogen can be renewable; produces a constant voltage; no toxic chemicals released after disposal; the only product is water.

Disadvantage, any one from: hydrogen is made from fossil fuels or non-renewable resources; hydrogen is difficult to store; hydrogen is flammable or explosive; costs more to refuel; costs more to manufacture; not many hydrogen filling stations.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the advantage and one for the disadvantage.

exam_phrases: fuel cells operate as long as reactants are supplied
voltage drops in chemical cells as reactants are used up
storage of hydrogen is difficult because it is a gas
fuel cells are expensive to manufacture

mistakes.wrong: Hydrogen and water react in a fuel cell to make oxygen.
mistakes.right: Hydrogen and oxygen react, and water is the only product: hydrogen + oxygen → water.

mistakes.wrong: Fuel cells are better than chemical cells.
mistakes.right: Give a conclusion with reasons. Either cell can be chosen, but suitable reasons must be given, and three points are needed for the top level.

worked_example.question:
Hydrogen-oxygen fuel cells can be used to provide electrical energy in a spacecraft.

The reaction that takes place in the fuel cell is
hydrogen + oxygen → water

Evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of providing electrical energy in a spacecraft using hydrogen-oxygen fuel cells rather than chemical cells.
answer_points: Advantages: once set up, fuel cells need no maintenance and work as long as reactants are supplied.
Chemical cells have a limited lifetime and need replacing, and the voltage drops as their reactants are used up.
Used chemical cells take up space and cannot be used again, or need recharging.
Water is the only product and can be used as drinking water.
Disadvantages: hydrogen and oxygen must be supplied in gas tanks, hydrogen is a gas that is difficult to store and is flammable, and fuel cells are expensive to manufacture.
Conclusion: either cell can be chosen, with suitable reasons, for example fuel cells are better because the water is useful and chemical cells run out.
worked_example.tip: This is a levels question. For the top level, describe three advantages or disadvantages and evaluate them to form a conclusion.

exam_phrases: refuelling time (for a fuel cell) is less
mass (of car) is less with a fuel cell

mistakes.wrong: The electric car takes 360 minutes and the fuel cell car takes 4 minutes.
mistakes.right: Just restating the data is ignored. Make a comparison: the fuel cell car takes 356 minutes less to refuel.
This is ignored. Use the data given: refuelling time, cost of refuelling, CO₂ emitted and mass of the car.

worked_example.question:
Car manufacturers are developing cars that are powered by hydrogen/oxygen fuel cells.

The table shows some information about a 200 km journey using an electric car and a car using a fuel cell.

Refuelling time in minutes: electric 360, fuel cell 4
Cost of refuelling in £: electric 3.20, fuel cell 4.20
CO₂ emitted in kg: electric 48, fuel cell 36
Mass of car in kg: electric 1550, fuel cell 1200

Evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of using a car powered by a fuel cell, rather than an electric car for the 200 km journey.
answer_points: Any two advantages of the fuel cell car, each as a comparison:
Refuelling time is less (4 minutes compared with 360 minutes).
It emits less CO₂ (36 kg compared with 48 kg).
The mass of the car is less (1200 kg compared with 1550 kg).
And a disadvantage: the cost of refuelling is more (£4.20 compared with £3.20).
worked_example.tip: Two advantages and one disadvantage, one mark each. Each must be a comparison, not a restatement of the data.
